hmmt-feb-2007-team2-01.prompt: Find the sum of the positive integer divisors of $2^{2007}$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-02.prompt: The four sides of quadrilateral $ABCD$ are equal in length. Determine the perimeter of $ABCD$ given that it has area $120$ and $AC=10$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-03.prompt: Five people are crowding into a booth against a wall at a noisy restaurant. If at most three can fit on one side, how many seating arrangements accommodate them all?

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-04.prompt: Thomas and Michael are just two people in a large pool of well qualified candidates for appointment to a problem writing committee for a prestigious college math contest. It is $40$ times more likely that both will serve if the size of the committee is increased from its traditional $3$ members to a whopping $n$ members. Determine $n$. (Each person in the pool is equally likely to be chosen.)

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-05.prompt: The curves $y=x^2(x-3)^2$ and $y=(x^2-1)(x-2)$ intersect at a number of points in the real plane. Determine the sum of the $x$-coordinates of these points of intersection.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-06.prompt: Andrew has a fair six-sided die labeled with $1$ through $6$ as usual. He tosses it repeatedly, and on every third roll writes down the number facing up as long as it is not the $6$. He stops as soon as the last two numbers he has written down are both squares or one is a prime and the other is a square. What is the probability that he stops after writing squares consecutively?

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-07.prompt: Three positive reals $x,y,z$ are such that $$x^2+2(y-1)(z-1)=85,\quad y^2+2(z-1)(x-1)=84,\quad z^2+2(x-1)(y-1)=89.$$ Compute $x+y+z$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-08.prompt: Find the positive real number(s) $x$ such that $\dfrac12\left(3x^2-1\right)=\left(x^2-50x-10\right)\left(x^2+25x+5\right)$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-09.prompt: Cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ has side lengths $AB=1$, $BC=2$, $CD=3$, and $AD=4$. Determine $AC/BD$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-10.prompt: A positive real number $x$ is such that $$\sqrt[3]{1-x^3}+\sqrt[3]{1+x^3}=1.$$ Find $x^2$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-11.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle (a *tangential* quadrilateral), with incenter $I$ (the center of the incircle). Since $I$ lies on the bisector of each angle, write $\angle DAB=2\alpha$, $\angle ABC=2\beta$, $\angle BCD=2\gamma$, $\angle CDA=2\delta$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=180^\circ$. Let $P$ be the point outside $ABCD$ (on the other side of $AB$ from $I$) such that triangle $PAB$ is similar to triangle $IDC$, with $P\leftrightarrow I$, $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow C$. Show that $PAIB$ is cyclic by proving that $\angle IAP$ is supplementary to $\angle PBI$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-12.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle (a *tangential* quadrilateral), with incenter $I$ (the center of the incircle). Since $I$ lies on the bisector of each angle, write $\angle DAB=2\alpha$, $\angle ABC=2\beta$, $\angle BCD=2\gamma$, $\angle CDA=2\delta$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=180^\circ$. Let $P$ be the point outside $ABCD$ (on the other side of $AB$ from $I$) such that triangle $PAB$ is similar to triangle $IDC$, with $P\leftrightarrow I$, $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow C$. You may use that $PAIB$ is cyclic. Show that triangle $PAI$ is similar to triangle $BIC$, and conclude that $$PA=\frac{PI}{BC}\cdot BI.$$
hmmt-feb-2007-team2-12.answer: $\triangle PAI\sim\triangle BIC$ (angles $\angle API=\angle IBC$, $\angle PIA=\angle BCI$), giving $PA/BI=PI/BC$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-13.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle (a *tangential* quadrilateral), with incenter $I$ (the center of the incircle). Since $I$ lies on the bisector of each angle, write $\angle DAB=2\alpha$, $\angle ABC=2\beta$, $\angle BCD=2\gamma$, $\angle CDA=2\delta$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=180^\circ$. Let $P$ be the point outside $ABCD$ (on the other side of $AB$ from $I$) such that triangle $PAB$ is similar to triangle $IDC$, with $P\leftrightarrow I$, $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow C$. You may use that $PAIB$ is cyclic and that $PA=\dfrac{PI}{BC}\cdot BI$. Deduce that $$\frac{BC}{AD}\cdot\frac{AI}{BI}\cdot\frac{DI}{CI}=1.$$
hmmt-feb-2007-team2-13.answer: Apply the same result with the roles $A\leftrightarrow B$, $C\leftrightarrow D$ swapped to get $PB=\frac{PI}{AD}\cdot AI$, then compare $PA/PB$ two ways.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-14.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle and incenter $I$. You may use (proved for every labeling of the vertices in cyclic order) that $\dfrac{BC}{AD}\cdot\dfrac{AI}{BI}\cdot\dfrac{DI}{CI}=1$. Show that $AB+CD=AD+BC$. Use this to conclude that for some positive number $\alpha$, $$AB=\alpha\left(\frac{AI}{CI}+\frac{BI}{DI}\right),\ BC=\alpha\left(\frac{BI}{DI}+\frac{CI}{AI}\right),\ CD=\alpha\left(\frac{CI}{AI}+\frac{DI}{BI}\right),\ DA=\alpha\left(\frac{DI}{BI}+\frac{AI}{CI}\right).$$
hmmt-feb-2007-team2-14.answer: Pitot: $AB+CD=AD+BC$ by equal tangents; the ratio $AB:BC:CD:DA$ is then forced, and the displayed values satisfy it.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-15.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle (a *tangential* quadrilateral), with incenter $I$ (the center of the incircle). Since $I$ lies on the bisector of each angle, write $\angle DAB=2\alpha$, $\angle ABC=2\beta$, $\angle BCD=2\gamma$, $\angle CDA=2\delta$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=180^\circ$. Let $P$ be the point outside $ABCD$ (on the other side of $AB$ from $I$) such that triangle $PAB$ is similar to triangle $IDC$, with $P\leftrightarrow I$, $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow C$. You may use that $PAIB$ is cyclic, that $PA=\dfrac{PI}{BC}\cdot BI$, that $PB=\dfrac{PI}{AD}\cdot AI$, and that $\dfrac{BC}{AD}\cdot\dfrac{AI}{BI}\cdot\dfrac{DI}{CI}=1$. Show that $$AB\cdot BC=BI^2+\frac{AI\cdot BI\cdot CI}{DI}.$$
hmmt-feb-2007-team2-15.answer: Ptolemy in $PAIB$: $AB\cdot PI=PA\cdot BI+PB\cdot AI$; substitute $PA$, $PB$ and $BC/AD$.

hmmt-feb-2007-team2-16.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with an incircle, tangent to sides $AB,BC,CD,DA$ at points $P,Q,R,S$ respectively. Show that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $PR\perp QS$.
hmmt-feb-2007-team2-16.answer: Angle chase with the tangent points: $\angle PTQ=180^\circ-\alpha-\beta$ where $\angle A=180^\circ-2\alpha$ and $\angle C=180^\circ-2\beta$; cyclic iff $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$.
